rules.quote: Spell out ordinal numbers from ‘first’ to ‘ninth’. Use numerals for ordinals from ‘10th’ onwards.
rules.violation_condition: an ordinal number from 1st to 9th written with numerals (e.g. '1st', '9th'), or an ordinal from 10th upwards written as words (e.g. 'tenth', 'twenty-first'), outside of allowed exceptions
when: Do not apply to centuries (e.g. '1st century', '9th century').
Do not apply to edition numbers in reference lists (e.g. '2nd edn').
Do not apply to official organisation names written with numerals (e.g. '1st Australian Infantry Battalion').
Very large rounded ordinals are spelled out in words with a suffix (e.g. 'millionth').
rules.why: G-1, G-2, G-4: 2ec0421dd2b9 states the base rule, consolidating the heading restatement and suffix list.

rules.violation_condition: an ordinal number suffix written in superscript (e.g. 10ᵗʰ)
rules.why: Specific distinct typography/accessibility requirement.

covers.quote: Exception to ordinals rule for centuries

parts.quote: In the 1st century CE, Tiberius succeeded Augustus Caesar as Roman emperor.
Vikings established a Norse kingdom around Dublin in the 9th century.
The gallery bought a 15th-century painting.

rules.quote: Use numerals, not words, when writing ordinals with centuries.
rules.violation_condition: a century ordinal below 10th spelled out in words (e.g. 'first century', 'ninth century')
rules.why: G-2/G-4: Specific actionable rule governing century ordinals.

rules.violation_condition: the word 'century' or 'centuries' written with initial capitalisation when referring to centuries (e.g. '21st Century')
when: Does not apply at the start of a sentence or where title casing is strictly required.
rules.why: Distinct casing rule for 'century' and 'centuries'.

rules.quote: Spell out the number and include the relevant suffix.

when: Applies to very large rounded ordinal numbers such as millionth, billionth.

rules.quote: In reference lists, use numerals with a suffix for editions of a publication.

rules.quote: If an organisation’s name includes a numeral, write the name as the organisation does.

covers.quote: Create a list rather than use ordinals
Always use numbered lists rather than ordinals when you’re expressing a series of items or steps – for example, in recommendations or instructions.

examples.note: Numbered list used instead of ordinals in running prose.

parts.quote: To apply for the grant:
complete the eligibility checklist
submit a business case
provide supporting documents.

examples.note: Ordinals used to order steps in running prose.

parts.quote: If you want to apply for the grant, first complete the eligibility checklist. Second, you must submit a business case; and third, you must provide supporting documents.

rules.quote: Don’t use ordinals to order points in general content.
rules.specification: Flag ordinals (first, second, third) used transitionally in running text to introduce successive items or instructions instead of using a numbered list or run-on list.
rules.violation_condition: using ordinals (e.g. 'first', 'second', 'third') in running prose to order a series of points, steps, or recommendations
when: Except when 'firstly' and 'secondly' are deliberately used as a pair in journal/report content.
rules.why: G-1, G-2, G-4: Consolidated general principle and recommendation instructions.

examples.note: Firstly and secondly used as a pair.

parts.quote: The committee responded in 2 ways. Firstly, they asked for an immediate adjournment of proceedings. Secondly, they sought clarification about their powers to subpoena witnesses.

rules.quote: ‘Firstly’ and ‘secondly’ work as a pair. Don’t use one without the other.
rules.violation_condition: using 'firstly' without 'secondly' or 'secondly' without 'firstly' to order thoughts
rules.why: G-2: Standalone rule governing pairing of firstly/secondly.

parts.quote: The committee took evidence from peak bodies, unions and the department.
The committee took evidence from, firstly, peak bodies; secondly, unions; and thirdly, the department.

rules.why: G-2: Direct clear prohibition of 'thirdly'.

parts.quote: 12 February 2020

rules.quote: Use numerals without a suffix for dates.
rules.violation_condition: a date written with an ordinal suffix on the day number (e.g. '12th February 2020')
rules.why: G-4: Heading restated in body sentence.

covers.quote: Use a non-breaking space for names with regnal numbers
